issue_context.title: 'systemd-analyze condition' fails on ConditionPathExistsGlob
issue_context.body:
**systemd version: 245/ 244**

**distribution: arch linux/ custom BSP**

`systemd-analyze condition 'ConditionPathExistsGlob=/usr/lib/systemd/system'`

However within a service [unit] the Condition itself worked

**Expected behaviour you didn't see**
```
test.service: ConditionPathExistsGlob=/usr/lib/systemd/system succeeded.
Conditions succeeded.
```
as it would have been without glob
`systemd-analyze condition 'ConditionPathExists=/usr/lib/systemd/system` 

**Unexpected behaviour you saw**
`Expected "=" in "ConditionPathExistsGlob=/usr/lib/systemd/system".`

**Steps to reproduce the problem**
see above.
At first I used a wildcard but the result is the same. Dropped wildcard "*" to be sure that my shell globbing is not the problem

review_comments: I was confused about why this works, but I see it's because the code uses `startswith()` to compare the condition name. Should we instead change it to use `streq()` so the ordering doesn't matter?
